notes.hold: The live-trading HOLD is unchanged. The two probes are the only things placing real orders — 1 contract each, $5 open-cost cap apiece.
notes.tape_a: Every dollar figure from a historical replay is a Tape-A artifact: fills there are a model, not a fact, and no strategy is promoted on Tape A alone. Quote cents per contract; never quote the bankroll.

bots.name: P8-CBFADE branch B
bots.one_line: Buys a pre-match favourite (p0>=0.60) that spiked to >=0.90 in play and has come back into 0.55-0.70, then rests a sell at 0.9500. Stakes 2% of equity per entry, capped by book depth.
bots.detail_note: Alex lifted the live-trading HOLD for this strategy on 2026-08-08 ("retire the probe and turn on the bot"). Same engine as the 1-contract probe, run with --sized; the probe was retired at cutover because one entry per match is enforced per-instrument and two instruments would enter the same match. SIZING: qty = floor(min(2% of equity, book depth at <=0.70, cash headroom, $400) / 0.70). Equity is venue cash + open positions at cost, re-read every cycle, so the stake tracks the real balance and needs no redeploy when the account is funded. ENVELOPE: 8 concurrent x 2% = ~16% peak exposure; 20% open-cost ceiling; $400 absolute per position; 24 entries/UTC-day; $50 equity floor. NO daily stop and NO bankroll floor (Alex's decision, 2026-08-08). WORTH: +2.40c/contract is the deployable claim, not the +7.04c raw EV — of the raw +5.53c net, +3.13c is the tape paying anyone who buys a favourite at 67-70c at first touch. Every historical figure is Tier 1s (no order book in the archive). The exit's real fill rate is n=5 from the probe. H1 remains sealed, 0 of 3 opens. STOP: touch ~/sportsbet/P8BOT_KILL (decommission). PAUSE: systemctl stop sportsbet-p8bot (resting exits survive by design).

bots.name: 004 buy-despair
bots.one_line: Armed at in-play mid ≤12¢, rested maker buys at 2/3/4/6¢, held to settlement.
why_stopped: Halted 2026-08-01 (live/KILL) and never restarted. Two things killed it, both found after go-live.

The backtest it was sized against was rented from hindsight: 159's `entry ≤ last_print − 1800s` filter is look-ahead, and the causal canary re-ran all 14 estimators over 71.3M trades — 90–99% of the headline vanishes at censor 0. The edge is ~+0.5¢/contract, not +6 to +8¢.

The live engine's out-guard was dead: it compared Kalshi's `close_time` (median 13.6 days past settlement) against a 30-minute window, so 44–64% of ladder fills landed in the final half hour of already-decided matches.

And the stop rule was unreachable anyway — detecting +0.56¢ against zero at 80% power needs ~9,095 ladders, about 1.8 years and ~$83,000 of burn. A forward P&L test cannot validate this strategy at this bankroll; only a cost cap makes sense.
bots.detail_note: Everything below is the engine's own record from its two live days, across both venues. It won nothing — and under the causal edge (a 4.3% win rate, not the ~11% it was sized on) a run of zero wins over this many settlements has probability around 0.3. It was never evidence of anything.

probes.name: Despair fill-rate probe
probes.measures: Do the V7 ladder rungs actually fill? Rests exactly 1 contract at 2/3/4/5/6¢ on markets V7 would arm, and records queue-at-placement, time-to-fill and mid markouts per order.
probes.why: Every V7 dollar figure is a Tier-1s replay artifact — the archive has no order book, so backtested fill rates are upper bounds. The 5¢ rung had never been observed at all before this instrument ran.
caveats: Probe P&L is an instrument cost and is excluded from every edge claim.
The v5_pass=1 strict subset is the population V7's economics actually rest on — read that table, not the soft-gate one.
rest_s is the denominator: a 0% rung that only ever rested 20s has not been measured, it has been interrupted.

probes.name: P8-CBFADE branch-B probe (RETIRED)
probes.measures: Does a resting maker sell at 0.9500 fill? Taker-buys 1 contract of a comeback favourite at ≤0.70, then rests a post-only sell at 0.9500 until it fills or the match settles.
probes.why: Branch B's entire +2.40¢/contract edge is that resting sell, and no historical tape has an order book — the assumption is untestable offline. It also measures whether the ≤0.70 entry was available at all.
caveats: RETIRED 2026-08-08 at the cutover to the sized bot. Final measurement: 3 of 5 exits filled at 0.9500 (both non-fills confirmed), median time-to-fill 703s, median queue at placement 542 contracts. Exchange verified flat at retirement — 0 resting, 0 positions.

The headline is an INTERVAL. A position that closes with no venue-reported fill is a confirmed non-fill only when the fills feed was healthy; otherwise it is unknown. A wide interval means fix the feed, not quote the lower bound.

The kill file is DECOMMISSION, not pause — a cancelled client_order_id is consumed forever, so kill-then-resume with an open position leaves it unhedgeable. Use `systemctl stop` to pause; exits survive it by design.
~5% of tour fixtures are invisible to API-Tennis and are omitted. That costs sample size; it is a bias only if coverage correlates with whether a 0.95 sell fills, which is unmeasured.

summary: First strategy through the three-branch fleshing protocol, and the first to break hold-to-settlement's five-strategy winning streak on the exit grid: A (hold) $16,326, B (sell @0.9500) $22,089, C (2h time stop) $13,414 — exactly the pre-registered ranking.

The headline is mostly the tape. A price-matched, one-per-match, first-touch random entry with the same exit earns +3.13¢ net with no signal in it at all. P8's rule is worth the difference: +2.40¢, and that figure is flat across fee, latency and print-size caps (+2.386 / +2.406 / +2.406 / +2.387), which is the strongest robustness statement this tape can produce.
Two independent fill models agree to 0.4% ($22,089 replaylite vs $22,178 chronological Tier-1s), and the censor multiplier is 0.96 — flat, no endgame rent.

Nothing after Stage 2 earned its way in: 96 conditions per branch → one survivor (a downweight, not a gate), 55 combinations → zero beat their own flat book in dollars, 15 levers → zero adopted. Stage 2 chose this strategy.
pipeline.next: The edge lives in a maker exit with no queue model — the p8b probe is measuring exactly that. Recommended promotion to Refinement as a forward-paper candidate is on the table but NOT done; quote +2.40¢, never +7.04¢.

pipeline.title: Despair: Polymarket vs Kalshi head-to-head
pipeline.one_line: Same despair ladder, both venues, same matches — which venue should it trade on?
headline: Kalshi (V7 fills)
+3.73¢
wk-t 4.79
Polymarket bare
−0.84¢
wk-t −4.94
PM + Kalshi shield
+1.22¢
wk-t ~2.0
summary: Kalshi wins decisively — roughly 3× per fill and 5–10× in total, at every accounting level. Despair does not port to Polymarket.

The verifier overturned the reason, and the overturn is the durable finding: the bare-PM loss is not live adverse selection, it is PM's dead-time penny tape. Fills within ~5 minutes of match end earn −3.26¢ at a 0.08% win rate — the tape keeps printing pennies after the match is decided and resting bids buy the corpses. Restricted to >10 minutes before the end, bare PM fills are already +1.12¢.
Also replicated here in an independent harness: V4's capacity-guard surprise. Adding the 800/800/400/200 per-order caps moved the ungated Kalshi replay from $1,487 to $14,336.
pipeline.next: Standing rule adopted: any PM resting-order idea needs a liveness veto first. A death-floor veto (pull only when Kalshi is below an absolute floor) is parked and needs pre-registration before it is touched.

summary: The mechanism is real and it is the first thing in this project that has separated informed from uninformed fills on the way down: at D=2¢ the veto would have blocked 86.8% of losing fills against 79.3% of winning ones, a 7.5-point gap at every rung, and shielded fills break the win≈price calibration that has killed every other resting-bid idea.
The money is gone. By quarter: +17.7 / +48.4 / +3.1 / −0.8¢ — Kalshi tennis's first months left wide slow divergences and they were competed away within about two quarters.

A verifier refutation was adopted on top: the headline latency cell's sign flips with the integer-second timestamp tie-break, so any condition read off that tape needs a deterministic tie rule — use the both-books MIN veto, which is stronger anyway.
pipeline.next: Cross-venue inefficiencies expire — date any cross-venue backtest before believing it. The unconditional defensive rule stands regardless of edge: never leave a resting PM tennis quote alive through a Kalshi move.

pipeline.title: Cross-venue lead-lag, Kalshi ↔ Polymarket
pipeline.one_line: Which venue moves first, and can the laggard be taken before it catches up?
headline: Kalshi leads by
3–9s
6× correlation asymmetry
Kalshi initiates
of ≥2¢ unilateral moves
executable edge
−0.67¢ net
gone within 5 seconds
summary: The first Kalshi↔PM tennis join ever built here (14,995 Kalshi matches, 5,986 matched, 26.2M prints) and it produced a clean market fact: Kalshi leads Polymarket tennis by about 3–9 seconds, initiating 88% of unilateral moves, with PM responding in a median 9s.
The timestamp-artifact objection was tested and refuted with a placebo event study — the cross-correlation alone cannot rule out clock skew, so reuse that design, not the CCF.

It is not executable. Paying the stale print reads +3.40¢ (the illusion); the next-print bracket is +0.25¢ gross and −0.67¢ net, and a 5-second delay takes it to zero. 92% of gaps converge, in prints you cannot have.
pipeline.next: Consequence for everything else: any PM maker strategy is quoting into a market Kalshi front-runs by seconds. That is a mandatory input to any dual-venue maker design.

summary: The first genuinely clean signal this project found — a flat censor curve, meaning no endgame rent — and it still did not survive contact with execution.

The resting-bid sweep killed the deployable version: all 11 rungs from 37¢ down to 27¢ earn between −0.9¢ and +0.2¢, every $800 replay ends below $800, and the win rate at bid X is ≈X at every level. The whole +2.43¢ lives in 352 gap-through fills the next-print model hands out free.

Then the corrected placebo took the rest: under a price-matched, one-per-match, first-touch null, FAV40's entry earns +2.44¢ against the null's +3.92¢ — an excess of −1.48¢. Buying a favourite at the same price in a random match beat waiting for the signal.
Its Stage-1 numbers are unaffected and reproduce exactly; it remains the harness reference. What is challenged is whether the entry rule does anything.
pipeline.next: Do not cite FAV40's EV as evidence of entry skill without re-testing it against the corrected placebo. Standing lesson from this run: for any taker-entry strategy, run the resting-bid bracket before believing next-print EV.

pipeline.title: Collapsed favourite, caught on the upswing
pipeline.one_line: Arm a collapsed favourite at ≤30¢, fire on a +5¢ rebound off the running low.
headline: EV gross / net
+2.15 / +1.10¢
t 1.31
pay the trigger
−0.25¢ net
one tick of slippage
conditions passing
0 of 88
nothing screened in
summary: Killed as unresolvable rather than refuted, and the distinction is the finding. The censor curve is clean (1.10×) and the trap everyone expected — endgame rent — is simply absent.

Execution kills it: the modelled fill lands 1.35¢ below the print that triggered it, and you cannot chase a rising price and be filled cheaper than the tick you chased. Pay the trigger and it is −0.25¢ net.

The method lesson outlived the strategy. P&L = won − q, so any comparison that does not hold entry price fixed is a price comparison in disguise — it destroyed two separate nulls in opposite directions before the right test (stratify into 2¢ buckets, compare settlement win rates) was found.
pipeline.next: The upswing question is not answerable from a trade tape where price and match state are entangled. It needs the recorder's book plus score state.

pipeline.title: Favourite drops to 25¢, bid 30¢, sell 45¢
pipeline.one_line: A 70¢ favourite falls to 25¢: rest a bid at 30¢, sell at 45¢.
headline: end to end
−8.50¢
t −10.08, n=632
win rate at 30¢ bid
so the bid loses by arithmetic

−2.06¢

summary: Two independent leaks, and the pipeline's own bracket rule caught both before any real work went in.
The bid loses by arithmetic, not statistics: the population it buys settles at a 24.53% win rate, so paying 30¢ is −5.47¢ on every fill. The identity reproduces the measured number to three decimals.
The exit caps winners and rescues no losers: 47.8% touch 45¢ and half of those would have won outright; the 330 that never touch it win 0.0% and eat the full stake anyway.
This is where the standing prior came from: Polymarket tennis is well priced on the way down. Two strategies on disjoint price bands both show win-rate-at-bid-X ≈ X for collapsing favourites.
pipeline.next: Any future 'buy the collapsing favourite at a resting bid' idea should be expected to fail. Run the resting-bid bracket first — it is one sweep and it kills or clears the idea.

pipeline.title: Ladder 30¢→15¢, sell +5¢ above each buy
pipeline.one_line: Buy every rung from 30¢ down to 15¢ and rest a sell 5¢ above each.
headline: pooled
−3.80¢
t −10.15, 10,051 fills
rungs below break-even
16 of 16

$800 replay
ruin
at 1%, 0.5% and 0.25%
summary: Rejectable on paper, and the arithmetic is worth keeping. At rung X you need the price to touch X+5 or you lose the full stake, so break-even is X/(X+5): 85.7% at the 30¢ rung. Observed: 75.1%, falling to 54.8% at 15¢. Max profit per full ladder is +80¢ against a −360¢ max loss.

It also produced a fingerprint worth checking for: 57.7% of ladders are profitable and the median ladder makes +20¢, but the mean is −54.7¢. When median and mean disagree in sign, suspect a grid martingale and check the payoff ratio before anything else.

The mechanism is adverse capital allocation by construction — a falling price fills more rungs, so 77.7% of deployed capital lands in matches that lose, and when the favourite does recover every rung sells at exactly +5¢, capping 100% of the upside.
pipeline.next: Standing rule: any multi-rung entry must be judged on capital-weighted outcomes, never per-rung averages — the rung count is itself correlated with the outcome.

summary: Raised by P8's own placebo. The Kalshi tennis tape has a standing bid for favourites at 67–70¢, and collecting it needs no rule whatsoever — it pays 57% of what P8-CBFADE branch B pays.

It is simpler than anything else in the ledger and it has never been screened: no censor sweep, no delay sweep, no resting-bid bracket, no quarters or time splits, no clean-room verification, no cross-venue check.
If it survives its own diagnostics it may be the better deployment, and P8 becomes a sizing overlay on it rather than a strategy in its own right.
pipeline.next: Screen it before more effort goes into refining P8. First test is the one that killed FAV40 and FAV25: the resting-bid bracket. A first-touch taker entry is exactly the shape whose modelled fill has flattered every predecessor into its grave.
